purpose: Check whether the directly related Philippine Caraga literature located for Johnius borneensis contains primary stomach-content or prey-composition evidence, while distinguishing a bounded search result from a claim that no such study exists.

discoveryQueries: Johnius borneensis stomach contents Philippines Agusan Butuan
Johnius borneensis feeding habits diet Philippines
Johnius borneensis gut content OR stomach content Philippines
Guama stomach contents feeding ecology Agusan Philippines
Johnius borneensis Agusan River diet prey

reviewedLocalPapers.title: Reproductive aspects of the native Sharpnose hammer croaker, Johnius borneensis (Bleeker, 1850) from Agusan River Estuary, Caraga region, Philippines
reviewedLocalPapers.scope: Agusan River Estuary; 223 fish examined February-April 2017; study measures reproductive biology and length-weight characteristics.
reviewedLocalPapers.dietFinding: The stated objectives, methods and reviewed article text concern reproductive measures; no stomach-content prey analysis or diet-composition result was located.

reviewedLocalPapers.title: Length-Weight Relationship (LWR), Gonadosomatic Index (GSI) and Fecundity of Johnius borneensis (Bleeker, 1850) from Lower Agusan River basin, Butuan City, Philippines
reviewedLocalPapers.scope: Lower Agusan River basin; 304 fish sampled May 2017-January 2018; study measures length-weight and reproductive characteristics.
reviewedLocalPapers.dietFinding: The stated objectives and methods concern length-weight, gonadosomatic index, sexual maturity, sex ratio and fecundity; no stomach-content prey analysis or diet-composition result was located.

reviewedLocalPapers.title: Levels of cadmium, copper, lead, nickel and mercury in the muscles of Guama Johnius borneensis and sediments in lower Agusan river basin, Pagatpatan, Butuan city, Philippines
reviewedLocalPapers.scope: Pagatpatan; direct capture and tissue/sediment metals study reviewed previously in national rollout step 341.
reviewedLocalPapers.dietFinding: The discussion's piscivory statement cites Sasaki (2001); the local study itself does not report stomach-content prey measurements.

discoveryLeadsOutsidePhilippines: A 2013 Goa University thesis with primary stomach-content analysis was located and queued for separate review; it is an India comparison, not Philippine evidence.
The 2022 Pabean Bay and Pattani Bay primary diet papers already reviewed in step 343 are Indonesia and Thailand studies, respectively.

finding.boundedResult: No Philippine primary gut-content or prey-composition study for Johnius borneensis was located in the search and three directly related Caraga papers reviewed for this step.
finding.interpretation: This is a limited literature-search outcome, not proof that no Philippine study exists. No local prey profile, diet percentages, diet-to-catch link, bait recommendation, or present-day occurrence is supported by these reproductive/contaminant papers.
finding.implication: Keep the diet display comparative-only for now. A locally sampled diet claim requires a Philippine primary study that actually analyzes stomach contents or another explicit diet method and identifies its population, period, sample and prey categories.

limitations: Search-engine discovery is not a complete review of all journals, university repositories, theses or non-indexed local publications.
The result applies to the named species and bounded query set only; it is not an absence statement for Caraga, the Philippines or other taxa.
The 2017 and 2020 local studies provide historical sampling/reproductive context but not prey evidence.
Comparative India, Indonesia, Thailand or Western Central Pacific findings must not be presented as an Agusan or Philippine population diet.
Natural diet is separate from angling bait, catchability, legal permission, current presence and safety.
nextAction: Review the located 2013 Goa University primary thesis for its sampling scope, direct diet method, species-specific results, denominator clarity and rights. Retain it as non-Philippine comparison only, then continue the Caraga freshwater species-source queue.
